definition: Converting an image from one domain to another while preserving structure — day to night, sketch to photo, map to satellite.
details: Converting an image from one domain to another while preserving structure — day to night, sketch to photo, map to satellite. Pix2pix and CycleGAN established the task; diffusion models now lead it.

explainer.lead: Image-to-image translation converts an image from one visual domain to another while keeping its underlying structure intact. It matters because it enables tasks like turning day scenes into night or sketches into photos without re-drawing them.

tiers.eli5: It's like tracing a picture but recoloring it in a different style, so a pencil sketch becomes a photo of the same scene.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train paired or unpaired generators to map domains, then check that structure is preserved rather than just style. A common pitfall is the generator hallucinating or dropping details when the domains differ too much.
tiers.paperLevel: Given an input image in domain A, a model learns a mapping to domain B such that structural content is preserved; CycleGAN adds a cycle-consistency loss to allow training without paired examples. Limits include difficulty with large structural changes and mode collapse.

explainer.example: A model trained on matched map and satellite images turns a hand-drawn street map into a realistic satellite view of the same road layout.
